title: Arkret Service Operation DTOs
description: Canonical request and response DTOs for service operations. OpenAPI components reference this artifact so SDK and conformance tooling use one schema source.

SelfGovernanceDependencyResolveRequest.description: Resolve exact typed non-Event governance dependencies. history_traversal_access is required only when ordinary visibility would not expose a dependency in the retained history cut.

PeerGovernanceDependencyResolveRequest.description: Without history_traversal_access this is ordinary authenticated federation dependency resolution for apply_seal. The optional pending-archive traversal branch is only the narrow retained-cut exception; member request replicas never grant it.

GovernanceDependencyResolveOutcome.description: Every canonical selector is accounted for exactly once. Returned and missing entries are sorted by (selector.kind UTF-8 bytes, JCS(selector) UTF-8 bytes). Each branch has one exact check: availability_receipt recomputes the registered full AvailabilityReceipt digest; authenticated_signer_resolution_evidence and minimal_metadata_mls_leaf_signer_evidence compute SHA-256 over the complete canonical evidence object. Each evidence object is at most 1 MiB. If the complete same-shape outcome exceeds min(request.byte_limit,8388608), the service returns limit_exceeded with no partial items or cursor; callers split selectors and retry. Unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing selectors share missing_selectors.

predecessor_refs.description: The exact current accepted Seal frontier, byte-wise ascending and duplicate-free.

event_digests.description: The exact accepted uncovered Control Event set the client intends to place in Seal.delta, byte-wise ascending and duplicate-free.

SealAvailabilityReceiptIssueRequest.description: PCR-only pre-sign request for the availability dependencies of one exact prospective successor Seal. The server, not the caller, chooses sealed_at.

availability_receipt_digests.description: Every and only full AvailabilityReceipt content digest the prospective Seal must commit, byte-wise ascending and duplicate-free.

governance_dependencies.description: Every and only issued AvailabilityReceipt plus its authenticated holder-signer evidence, sorted by canonical selector order.

SealAvailabilityReceiptIssueOutcome.description: Exact PCR availability preparation. The client MUST verify request echo, canonical ordering, dependency content addresses and receipt coverage, then copy sealed_at and availability_receipt_digests unchanged into the signed Seal.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

ActorAggregateFrontierView.description: Read-only actor history aggregate. It has no single sequence or head and cannot be used for Event authoring.

frontiers.description: Visible Realm frontiers sorted by realm_id with no duplicate realm_id.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

auth_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

AuthSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ak.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

AuthorizationLeaseIssueIntent.description: Typed authorization target for a registered non-Event operation. The issuer rederives the current authority policy from the accepted basis; this object is not itself an authorization.

AuthorizationLeaseIssueOutcome.description: One authority-issued publication lease per requested Event, preserving request order.

AuthorizationLeaseIssueRequestBody.description: Exactly one non-empty target array: final signed Events for publication pre-admission, or typed non-Event operation intents. Mixed requests are forbidden.

AuthzCheckOutcome.description: ak.self.authz.read.check.v1 diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This shape may include freshness and obligation hints, but any obligation that affects reducer admission or external state MUST be re-issued and signed through PolicyCheckOutcome.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are Policy Server-mediated soft outcomes (the request enters async review). Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Frontier freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.

last_known_frontier_age_ms.description: Age of the newest revocation/auth frontier evidence used for this decision. Present when freshness_state is stale or unknown.

notary_status.description: Coarse status of the notary/frontier source used to diagnose stale or unknown revocation freshness.

reason_code.description: Registered reason code. High-risk stale or unknown revocation freshness returns revocation_freshness_unknown.

retry_after_ms.description: Set when `freshness_state ∈ {stale,unknown}` or a retryable `reason_code` is present; client SHOULD back off this amount before retry.

obligations.description: Policy server obligations (challenge / rate_limit / drop_attachment) the caller MUST satisfy before the action proceeds.

AuthzCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.authz.read.check.v1 input — local capability projection / preflight / diagnostic query. `resource` is optional because some actions (e.g. `ak.realm.create`, identity-scoped actions) have no Realm-bound target. The result is not a signed Policy Server decision and MUST NOT be used as Event auth_context, reducer accept proof, or cross-service authorization fact; dynamic policy obligations use ak.self.policy.read.check.v1.

actor_id.description: Subject did_core_id whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, frontier reference, request metadata.

uri.description: Fully-qualified URL clients can pass to browser primitives. Contains the `presign` query parameter, `blob_ref`, and a presign envelope bound to `realm_id` for Realm-owned blobs.

expires_at.description: Server-determined expiry; SHOULD be earlier than `now() + max_age_seconds`.

blob_ref.description: Target blob. MUST be a content-addressed ref or visible blob metadata id.

realm_id.description: Realm binding for Realm-owned blobs. Servers MUST include the same realm_id in the presign envelope and reject mismatches with blob metadata; only deployment-public/global blobs may omit this field.

max_age_seconds.description: Client-requested TTL upper bound. Server clamps to the smaller of this value, the issuing grant's `blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds` constraint, and the deployment-level cap.

purpose.description: Intended rendering / download mode. Servers MAY apply purpose-specific Content-Disposition or rate limits.

backend_token.description: Closed branch selected by backend_kind: arkret_native uses the typed signature object; every other v1 backend uses a non-empty opaque string.

participant_id.description: SFU-local short handle, scope `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`. UUIDv7-form rtc_participant typed ID.

backend_kind.description: Backend binding type identifier (livekit / arkret_native / etc.).

device_id.description: Stable protocol endpoint identifier. REQUIRED for agent_key_proof and covered by request_canonical_digest; the Account Authority MUST persist and return the same value in the issued grant so Principal Servers can bind MLS KeyPackage ownership, Welcome routing, consume/revoke operations, refresh, and restart recovery to one endpoint. It MUST NOT be derived from a session or grant id.

decisions.description: Verified signed decision chain in ascending defer_count order. Signed-reject is terminal and therefore does not remain in pending_proposals.

device_revocation_state.description: Present when this pending proposal is ak.device.revoke. It exposes the exact authority/device/generation binding and the universal action gate; it is reducer-derived and never copied from producer payload.

retained_faults.description: Deadline faults retained after a late but otherwise valid Seal is accepted. Sorted by (accepted_at, proposal_digest); this is evidence derived from the signed chain, not a second finality source.

device_message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity copied unchanged into DeviceMessageEnvelope.device_message_id. Reusing the same sender-scoped device_message_id with different canonical target content MUST fail with duplicate_conflict (reason device_message_id_conflict).

pruned_count.description: Number of queued messages actually deleted by this acknowledgement; zero is the legal result for a repeated or older acknowledgement token.

ack_token.description: Acknowledgement token previously issued to the same (principal_id, device_id) via an account subscribe to_device batch or a device_messages get page. Acknowledgement is cumulative and monotonic: the server prunes all delivered messages up to and including the token's bound queue position. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens MUST be rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything. Naturally idempotent; no Idempotency-Key required.

messages.description: DeviceMessageEnvelope items; not Event Envelope objects. This endpoint does not serve the durable Event timeline.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Covers this page plus all previously delivered messages for the authenticated device. Queue deletion happens only through ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1 with this token, never through the after= read cursor (client-sync.md §10.1).

next_cursor.description: Read-only continuation position; advancing it MUST NOT delete queued messages.

lost.description: SHOULD be true when unacknowledged messages were dropped (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position; clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths.

delivered.description: Principal-id to device-id map for messages accepted for delivery.

unknown_devices.description: Principal-id to device-id map for targets that were not deliverable.

accepted_at.description: Stable registry decision time for this exact accepted or duplicate operation. A duplicate returns the original acceptance time.

seq.description: New method sequence number when available.

did_method.description: DID method discriminator without the did: prefix (e.g. web, webvh, key). It MUST exactly equal the method component of did; verifiers dispatch method-specific validation only after that equality check.

seq.description: Optional method sequence number when the DID method exposes one.

prev_event_digest.description: Optional previous operation hash / key-log head, when required by the DID method.

operation.description: Complete DID method-native operation, including every controller/update/recovery proof required by that method. This is not a generic JSON Patch. The selected adapter MUST validate the immutable native operation and its full history before any state mutation; transport authentication never substitutes for method-native control proof.

DirectConversationFoundingAuthorityEvide.description: Closed XOR authorization evidence for one Direct Conversation founding unit, matching the two registered ak.realm.create admission variants. The human branch feeds direct_conversation_genesis; the controller_agent branch feeds direct_conversation_agent_genesis. Carrying both, neither, or mixed branch fields rejects the whole unit.

contact_round_evidence.description: Portable evidence for the pair's current Contact round. The verifier re-derives founder from the root Contact round, never from the current round.

contact_round_continuity_chains.description: Ordered tombstone/recontact predecessors from the current Contact round back to the pair's unique root Contact round, each linked by previous_terminal_contact_round_id. An empty array means the current round is itself the root. A break, a cycle, multiple roots or two directional proofs yielding different roots reject the unit.

agent_provision_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted Agent provision Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel agent_provision_digest is carried.

DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceOutc.description: Closed outcome of the direct_conversation_founding request branch. status is accepted for the first admission of this unit and duplicate for a byte-identical replay; partial is structurally impossible because the unit is atomic. A slot already closed by a different unit for the same pair returns the slot_already_committed error instead of this outcome.

event_ids.description: The four accepted Event IDs in the same wire order as the request. They are the exact preimage of receipt.founding_unit_digest.

DirectConversationFoundingFederationSubm.description: Direct Conversation founding exception branch of ak.peer.events.command.submit.v1 (zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4). The Realm does not yet exist at the receiver, so no ordinary federation_peer authority and no Realm-scoped service_binding_ref can be computed; destination binding comes from the section 3 service DID and trust-domain headers plus the source acceptance receipt. This is a registered atomic unit: a missing bounded dependency returns top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes and never a per-item partial.

events.description: The same four founder-signed Events in the same fixed wire order, byte-identical to what the source accepted.

DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission.description: Caller-authored Direct Conversation founding unit submitted to the founder's current Principal Server. The founder authors all four Events itself: realm_id is retype(events[0] Event ID) and main_strand_id is retype(events[2] Event ID), so no party can allocate either coordinate before the canonical preimage exists. The service never allocates, replaces or renegotiates an ID; it only verifies the unit, CAS-closes its local (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot and accepts zero or four Events atomically. See zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md sections 5.5 and 6.1.

unit_kind.description: Explicit discriminator. Ordinary single and batch submissions forbid this property, so the three request branches are an exact XOR.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key. The same key with the same founding unit replays the byte-identical receipt without advancing accepted_at; the same key with a different unit is duplicate_conflict with zero writes.

events.description: Exactly four founder-signed Events in fixed wire order: ak.realm.create with an omitted realm_id and a realm_genesis scope_ref, the peer participant's ak.member.state{join}, ak.strand.create with an omitted strand_id, then the founder's explicit ak.member.state{join} genesis write carrying head_eq null. Reordering, a fifth Event, either missing member join and a missing Strand each reject the whole unit.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Optional receiver-relative dependency bundles for the unit's seal_ref or seal_basis leaves. Bundles are transport evidence, not Event fields.

DirectoryGovernanceProof.description: Single resource-governance authorization proof for directory write surfaces (withdraw, takedown_appeal). Reuses the generic non-Event detached-JWS wire leaf while closing audience, purpose, and domain choices for this object family; canonical binding, signer authority, and freshness rules are defined in discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

discovery_event.description: The accepted ak.{kind}.discovery Event itself, delivered in its original signed form exactly as peer contact delivery carries the original ak.contact.* Event. resource_kind is derived from Event kind; resource_id is derived from the signed Event subject mapping. The Event's own proofs carry the resource governance signature, so no second signed copy of the same fact is defined (discovery-directory.md 8.3).

DirectoryTakedownAppealOutcome.description: Signed decision receipt acknowledging an appeal submission per discovery-directory.md §8.7 step 3.

appeal_id.description: Directory-local audit reference for the appeal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID. The payload segment excludes `:` so the value can neither begin with nor embed the ak: typed-ID namespace before the kind is registered.

decision_receipt.description: Signed Directory decision receipt; status pending until adjudicated.

DirectoryTakedownAppealRequestBody.description: Resource-side appeal packet against an operator takedown; the bound fields and governance signature are normative per discovery-directory.md §8.7.

takedown_id.description: The operator takedown_id from the takedown notice. The payload segment excludes `:` so the value can neither begin with nor embed the ak: typed-ID namespace before the kind is registered.

argument_digest.description: Digest of the appeal argument / evidence bundle (sha256:<hex>).

governance_proof.description: Signature by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate, equivalent strength to withdraw.governance_proof; wire form and binding per discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

withdrawal_ref.description: Directory-local audit reference for the withdrawal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID.

governance_proof.description: Signature proof by the resource governance key, equivalent strength to announce.discovery_state.proof; wire form and binding per discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

EventFederationSubmission.description: Event publication transported between peers. Online federation carries an empty ingress_receipts array and no authorization_lease; explicit delayed/offline federation carries its lease and one or more lease-bound receipts. The receiving peer independently revalidates the Event, current admission, optional delayed evidence and CBA closure.

control_proposal_ack.description: Canonical external-authority receipt set for a federated Control Move. Forbidden for DataEvents.

EventInitialSubmission.description: Initial durable Event publication. Online submission requires only the complete signed Event and performs current-state admission atomically. authorization_lease is optional and valid only for an explicitly requested delayed/offline publication window. Lease and dependency bundles are excluded from the Event digest.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Optional receiver-relative dependency bundles for the Event seal_ref or seal_basis. Bundles are transport evidence, not Event fields.

control_proposal_ack.description: Required external-authority receipt set when a Control Move is submitted to a receiver that cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum. Forbidden for DataEvents.

EventReadRow.description: A readable event item. Complete EventEnvelope is the only reducer input shape. RedactedEventView and ReferenceLockedEventStub are projection/completeness evidence for callers that may know the source event exists but may not receive its full canonical payload bytes.

SealSubmitOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.seals.command.submit.v1 after full Seal and active-device verification. A Seal is not an Event and never uses EventInitialSubmission.

accepted_event_digests.description: The Control Events this Seal accepted, as a set: byte-wise ascending and unique, the same normalization Seal.delta carries. Order MUST NOT be read as reducer apply order, which is causal-then-digest-descending and is not observable on this response; a client comparing this array against its own submission order or against a server's apply order is comparing two different sequences.

allOf.description: Actor-supplied ak.self.events.command.submit.v1 input envelope. It reuses the base Event shape, including the required producer-signed scope_ref, and forbids the sole reducer-stamped Event field actor_kind. Object payload schemas independently forbid actor-supplied effective_scope where that name is reserved for a read-only materialized object projection.

EventView.description: Result of ak.self.events.resource.get.v1 — a single complete Event Envelope, RedactedEventView, or ReferenceLockedEventStub with optional visibility / receipt hints. Redacted / locked variants are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be used as reducer input.

visibility.description: Caller-visible policy hint for this event (history visibility class, E2EE envelope class).

receipts.description: Event batch receipts witnessing this event, if visible.

EventsActorCasConflictProblem.description: Closed details for an authenticated, visible actor-chain cas_conflict that proves the submitted Event was not accepted and its signed basis is stale.

EventsDependencyMissingProblem.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for an atomic federation unit rejected with top-level dependency_missing. The unit performed zero Event, Seal, reducer, projection, or frontier writes.

EventsFrontierState.description: Account-client ak.self.events.read.frontier.v1 response for actor/data Event causal frontiers only. Realm Seal discovery is exclusively ak.self.seals.read.frontier.v1.

EventsFrontierFederationPeerState.description: Federation peer ak.peer.events.read.frontier.v1 response. Requires S2S signed trust-domain headers.

head_ids.description: Current federation-visible head Event IDs for this Realm.

max_hlc.description: Maximum HLC observed by the issuer at this frontier, when available.

frontier_root.description: Hash commitment returned to an authorized federation peer.

auth_state_root.description: Issuer-local authorization-state commitment for the actor_id named by the request. Present exactly when actor_id is supplied.

policy_frontier_root.description: Filtered policy-cell state root for the requested Realm. Present exactly when actor_id is supplied.

membership_frontier_root.description: Filtered membership and role state root for the actor_id named by the request. Present exactly when actor_id is supplied.

actor_seq_upper_bounds.description: Per-actor sequence upper bounds returned to an authorized federation peer.

witness_receipts.description: Optional witness or receipt-service attestations over the observed frontier.

signature.description: Service signature over the peer frontier response.

EventsFrontierRequestBody.description: QUERY content for ak.self.events.read.frontier.v1. actor_id is mandatory because this surface exposes only actor/data Event causal frontiers; use ak.self.seals.read.frontier.v1 for a Realm Seal frontier.

actor_id.description: Optional actor scope for policy-check authorization, policy, and membership roots. Generic federation probes omit it.

SealFrontierRequestBody.description: Canonical self/peer Realm Seal-frontier query. It never selects Event actor heads.

SealFrontierState.description: Self Seal discovery result. Managed Agent PCR successor-authoring receipts live here, never on the Event frontier surface.

PeerSealFrontierState.description: Authenticated peer Seal discovery result. The proof covers the complete frontier including its observation coordinate.

SealResolveRequestCore.description: Exact Seal-only resolve core. Event ids/digests are forbidden and remain on Event resolve.

SelfSealResolveRequestBody.description: Self Seal resolve. Optional history_traversal_access is the only history-recovery exception to ordinary visibility. Every selected Seal must lie in the retained target-to-base cut derived from the named durable request receipt or archive replica.

PeerSealResolveRequestBody.description: Authenticated peer Seal resolve. Optional history_traversal_access is checked against the exact retained request/archive-replica cut before lookup. Unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing are indistinguishable.

SealResolveOutcome.description: Every canonical input selector is accounted for exactly once by a verified Seal or same-shape missing ref. Returned Seals are sorted by seal_ref. Unknown and unauthorized are indistinguishable; no Event is returned.

EventsQueryOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.events.read.scan.v1. Ordering follows the "近邻先返回" rule unless `order` was explicitly set on the request; see service-http-binding.md §3.3.3.

prev_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward older events; pass to next request's `before=`.

next_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward newer events; pass to next request's `after=`.

has_more.description: True if more events remain in the `prev_cursor` (older) direction; SHOULD ignore `next_cursor` direction (subscribe / poll instead).

range_completeness.description: Optional. Present only when the request set include_completeness=true, the service advertises events_query_range_completeness, and at least one ak.attestation.range_completeness attestation covers the returned page's range (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Absence means the range is un-attested — neither an error nor a completeness confirmation. Clients verify per operations-sync.md §6.4.4 (root recompute, actor_seq_ranges check, witness_disagreement fail-closed).

attestation_refs.description: Event ids of ak.attestation.range_completeness events whose union of scopes covers the returned page. Over-coverage is legal; clients intersect scopes during verification.

attestations.description: Optional inline complete ak.attestation.range_completeness EventEnvelope objects for the referenced attestations. Every inline event's event_id MUST appear in attestation_refs and clients MUST verify the EventEnvelope signature / event_digest before using its payload. Servers MAY omit this field and let clients backfill the attestation events by id.

EventsQueryPostRequestBody.description: QUERY content for ak.self.events.read.scan.v1 and ak.peer.events.read.scan.v1.

realm_ids.description: Filter by Realm IDs. UNION within, intersection with `actor_ids[]`.

actor_ids.description: Filter by Actor DIDs. UNION within, intersection with `realm_ids[]`.

before.description: Return events strictly older than this cursor position (exclusive).

after.description: Return events strictly newer than this cursor position (exclusive).

order.description: Same semantics as the GET form `order` query parameter.

include_completeness.description: Request range-completeness attestation references covering the returned page (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Only effective when the service advertises ak.feature.events_query_range_completeness.v1 in supported_features; services that do not advertise it MUST ignore this parameter.

EventsResolveOutcome.description: ak.self.events.read.resolve.v1 result. events[] and missing[] plus optional unauthorized[] form a partition. This surface returns Event bytes only. Control-Move effectiveness is established separately from the complete current Seal frontier/resolve closure; no covering or first-activation Seal is attached. DataEvents carry their accepted seal_ref, never enter Seal.delta and never require a covering Seal.

missing.description: IDs / hashes that were requested but do not exist or are not visible (indistinguishable per visibility rules).

unauthorized.description: Optional split of missing into a separately-named bucket when policy explicitly distinguishes auth failure from non-existence.

EventsResolveRequestBody.description: ak.self.events.read.resolve.v1 request body. At least one of event_ids or event_digests must be non-empty. Standalone Seal selectors and Control-Move effectiveness checks belong only to the Seal frontier/resolve surfaces; this operation never attaches activation Seals.

history_traversal_access.description: Optional narrow access to Control Moves and registered apply_seal dependencies in the exact retained target-to-base traversal cut. It never authorizes unrelated DataEvents or timeline scanning; unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing remain same-shape.

max_response_bytes.description: Caller response budget, bounded by the service-advertised and 8 MiB canonical response ceilings.

AgentMembershipCascadeSubmission.description: Registered atomic/split Native Agent membership cascade unit. The receiver derives the exact Agent set from the controller terminal Event pre-state; the request cannot choose that set by omission or addition.

AgentMembershipCascadeFederationSubmissi.description: Federation form of the registered Native Agent cascade unit. Every nested Event already carries its origin Principal Server admission proof; the destination replays the same exact-set and atomicity rules.

EventsSubmitBatchRequestBody.description: Batch ak.self.events.command.submit.v1 request used by account clients.

EventsSubmitFederationBatchRequestBody.description: Ordinary Realm-scoped federation service-to-service ak.peer.events.command.submit.v1 request body. Each Event must contain its original principal_server_admission proof; the receiver validates it in-envelope and accepts no signer-key evidence sidecar.
